#3737. Call of Duty Endowment marks Remembrance Day with veterans' Valor Pack push

The Call of Duty Endowment is marking Remembrance Day and its 17th anniversary by encouraging Modern Warfare 4 and Warzone players to pick up its Valor Pack, with all of Activision's net proceeds going towards helping veterans find jobs.

The Call of Duty Endowment Valor Pack - which has been available since Modern Warfare 4 launched on 23rd October - was designed by the Endowment and Infinity Ward with US Marine Corps veteran and Medal of Honor recipient Kyle Carpenter in mind.

The items include a melee weapon blueprint inscribed with "Worth Fighting For", plus items called Relentless and Still Standing.

According to the Call of Duty blog, 100 percent of Activision's net proceeds from the pack (after VAT and sales tax) go to the Endowment.

To mark Remembrance Day, players who owned it and launched either game before 6pm GMT on 12th November also received double XP tokens and a DMZ survival kit.

"Veterans bring incredible skills into the workplace after military service," said Carpenter.

The Endowment, which supports veterans in the UK as well as the US, says it has now helped place more than 180,000 into "high-quality jobs", and wants to reach 200,000 by 2030.

Other partners are also raising money, with Pilot's round-up campaign raising more than £4.7 million ($6 million) for the Endowment since 2019. Polaris will also donate around £19,500 ($25,000) if players collectively complete 5 million rides in its DAGOR vehicle across Modern Warfare 4 and Warzone by 25th November.

It comes two weeks after Activision apologised to bereaved families of the Itaewon crowd crush victims and confirmed it would remove real footage of the tragedy from Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4. Players discovered that the game's opening cinematic uses short news clips to depict fictional civilian casualties during a North Korean invasion of South Korea. Those clips have since been found to include archive footage from the 2022 Itaewon disaster, in which around 160 people died.

#3736. Former Dishonored designer joins the team on New Blood's Victorian immersive sim Gloomwood, with a new level and new weapons coming this year

Gloomwood, the Victorian survival horror immersive sim (or, wait, I'm getting reports that we shouldn't call it an immersive sim, apparently) by Dillon Rogers is a game that is quite happily inspired by its predecessors such as Thief, Resident Evil and Dishonored; you could call it 'Thief with guns', if you really wanted to. (Sorry, I've just seen that the domain for Gloomwood's site used to be 'residenthievil.com'. Wonderful). Now, that last inspiration has come full circle, as publisher New Blood Interactive's latest update post confirms that the newest member of the team is none other than former Dishonored designer Julien Eveillé.

In addition to his work at Arkane on Dishonored and its sequel, Deathloop, and even Marvel's Blade, Eveillé also developed his own indie horror, 2024's short and sweet Threshold. It's quite a legacy to add to this team, and his hiring is described by New Blood as an example of how "finding level designers who are up to the task of working on Gloomwood is not easy". The post also mentions that Eveillé will be added alongside "our new devs", implying that he's not the only new addition to the team.

Other than these new hires, the update is set to include quite a bit to change up Gloomwood and make it bigger. The highlight is the First National Bank level, which is described as "our largest and most intricately designed level yet", with the screenshots showing off a grand and imposing, yet claustrophobic in places, that makes the act of going to the bank even more intimidating than usual. The Bank is joined by the new stun prod weapon, which is self-explanatory, and the new Rat and Fishdog transformations, which let you sneak through crawlspaces and swim through dirtied waters respectively. That sneaking will be made more difficult by the addition of alarms and blood pools that both alert surrounding guards to your presence, though the new Crow King transformation offers a new, acid-belching way to take down any guards that come running.

The update is tentatively scheduled for "before the end of the year", but New Blood aren't setting down a specific release date. Rogers himself will also be going through back surgery very soon, for which I wish him a gentle recovery and, hopefully, as easy a return to work as possible.

#3735. Hakoniwa Electric launches November 30

Hakoniwa Electric, a cozy puzzle exploration game about fixing electrical problems, will launch for PC via Steam on November 30 at 7:00 a.m. PT / 10:00 a.m. ET for 600 yen, developer Anettai announced. It will support English, Japanese, Korean, Traditional Chinese, and Simplified Chinese language options.

Here is an overview of the game, via its Steam page:

Hakoniwa Electric is a cute relaxing puzzle game. Explore adorable isometric stages, solve puzzles, and light them up. Why not spend a leisurely year as Akari, who’s taken over grandpa’s electronics shop, helping with the monthly troubles from the townsfolk?

Hakoniwa Electric is a relaxing isometric puzzle exploration game where you can unwind at your own pace.

Akari and her robot buddy Lamp take over grandpa’s electronics shop while he’s off vacationing in the tropics.

Light up the store, put up those job posters, and you’re good to go!

Tackle the little everyday woes from the townsfolk, and enjoy watching the seasons roll by and the shop slowly come alive over the course of a year.

Explore a charming little isometric world that captures the changing seasons.

Each stage is packed with delightful details just waiting for you to discover.

Wiring Puzzles Tucked Away in Cute Isometric Stages

Every stage hides a puzzle. Spot it, click to rotate the circuit pieces, and connect the wires.

No tough trial-and-error or math required—just gaze at the cuteness and relax in your own time.

Clear a stage, and Akari’s “Monthly Diary” updates with glimpses of her daily life. Peek in to see what she felt in that place and who she met…

I'm modding GTA 5 every day in a quest to either transform it into a PC version of GTA 6 or break it entirely. Come back tomorrow to find out what new horrible thing I've done to Rockstar's baby, or check out what I got up to earlier.

Right, I've had it. I have been rolled out like bread dough by errant minivans one too many times, and I've decided to do something about it. I am abolishing cars (within a very specific radius, sometimes).

Cycletopia – Replace cars with bicycles is a Grand Theft Auto 5 mod that does the thing it says in its title, which I wrote just there. All cars within a certain radius (I never figured out what radius, exactly, but there was definitely one involved) will, at the touch of a button, transmogrify into bicycles.

They will also, quite often, take flight, owing to some confusion regarding the laws of physics, leading to a hundred different iterations of that one bit from ET.

They are also all ridden by Franklin, since the button to turn on Bike World is the same button that turns the world's pedestrians into carbon copies of your player character. You'll tap the button and, nary moments later, hear "Aw shit!" as your doppelganger gaily endos down the freeway.

It is a nicer, quieter city. Gone are the vrrms of engines and the kablooeys of explosions that now make up the aural world of my modded Los Santos. In their place is the whirr of pedals and the occasional bell, with some allowances having to be made for Franklin's commentary, which is frequent and ribald. I hope this is what GTA 6 is like. Probably it will be.

#3733. Embracer begin yet another round of layoffs at Crystal Dynamics, while they're still midway through development on two Tomb Raider games

Update: Studio confirms eight staff lost their jobs

Update 18/11: Crystal Dynamics have provided the following statement to RPS, confirming it cut eight staff members:

As initially reported by Vertical Slice (thanks, Chris!), the workforce of Tomb Raider studio Crystal Dynamics is being cut as part of a new set of layoffs by owners Embracer. As far as is currently known, those affected include senior game designer Joshua Mitchell, senior environment technical artist Kevin Baker, and UI software engineer Garin R. K. Richards, all of whom shared news of their redunancies on LinkedIn. There may be more affected, but neither Crystal Dynamics nor Embracer have offered comments on the reduction of staff as yet.

This now marks the studio's fifth round of layoffs since Embracer acquired it in 2022, following cuts in March 2025, August 2025, November 2025, and March this year. This is a drastic amount even considering the current state of the industry, with layoffs seemingly happening several times a week, but unfortunately, this is par for the course for Embracer. Even still, it makes one wonder just how many staff are left at Crystal Dynamics by now. Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis and Tomb Raider: Catalyst are still in production, so you'd hope that the studio won't be shuttered entirely.

According to Legacy of Atlantis' Steam page, generative AI has been used in the development of Legacy of Atlantis "to support some early exploration and temporary development content. Any AI-assisted assets were either replaced or refined by humans in order to maintain the creative and artistic vision of the development team." I would hope that this isn't a case of Embracer cutting staff in the misguided hope that they can just be replaced with the use of genAI, but who can say. Solidarity to those affected, who I hope can find new work soon.

#3732. Ubisoft is reportedly making a new Rainbow Six Vegas game, nearly two decades after Vegas 2

Ubisoft is reportedly working on a new Rainbow Six Vegas game 18 years after the last entry in the series.

According to Insider Gaming, the project is in early development at Ubisoft Montreal under the codename Spades. It’s one of three new projects reportedly in production at the studio, and sources suggest a second of those is also set in the Rainbow Six universe. Eurogamer hasn’t been able to verify the report.

It’s not yet clear what form the new game will take, but Insider Gaming’s sources said it's "likely Vegas 3 rather than a remake" of an existing game. Insider Gaming expects it will be several years before Ubisoft officially announces a new Vegas game.

Rainbow Six Vegas launched in 2006, followed by Rainbow Six Vegas 2 in 2008. Since then, the series has centred on 2015's Rainbow Six Siege, and in August, Ubisoft announced Rainbow Six Tactics, a single-player, turn-based spin-off from Ubisoft Paris due in 2027.

Rainbow Six now sits under Vantage Studios, the Ubisoft subsidiary set up last year that also oversees Assassin’s Creed and Far Cry, and in which Tencent holds a 26.32 percent stake.

Last week, we learned that Ubisoft is reportedly working on two new Assassin's Creed games: one set in ancient Rome, and a mobile spin-off set in Jerusalem. The leak came less than a week after Ubisoft issued a statement about the future of the Assassin's Creed series, insisting there are currently no new remakes of the series' past games in the works.

This simple switch-up to my desk has made a massive difference

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

I've pretty much always carried an annoying, tense pain on the right side of my neck. And when I say always, I'm 29, and I remember going to see a physiotherapist about it when I was 18 - so you're talking my entire adult life. I tried everything: workouts, stretches, posture improvements, so you can probably imagine the mocking laugh that came out of me when, earlier this year, an ergonomics doctor at the Secretlab HQ told me all I needed was to switch my monitors around a bit.

But I should have had more faith in this sage, sage advice, because (alongside a renewed exercise routine to support it), the simple change to my setup actually did make a massive difference to my shoulder and neck pain. The only issue? The Secretlab products I needed to make it happen aren't the cheapest, but since they're now seeing discounts in the Black Friday Secretlab sale, I figure it's a good time to tell the story.

The TLDR here is that Secretlab's Vertical Monitor stand was all I needed to stop the constant strain of tension in my neck. If you want to skip the story and check it out on your own, it's available now in Secretlab's Black Friday or End-of-Year sale.

I met Dr. Lindsey “GamerDoc” Migliore at the Secretlab Singapore office back in April when I was invited to get a special early look at the then unannounced Secretlab Atlas. Myself and a few other UK journos were treated to an ergonomics session with Dr. Lindsey, a licensed physician and Esports medicine specialist who works with Esports athletes and organizations to optimize health and performance across both competitive and casual gaming.

Throughout the session, she made her way around the group, giving us a free clinic of sorts as we asked about our aches and pains and how we might improve our setups to remedy them. She roasted PCGamer's Jacob Ridley over his sitting position, but Secretlab's PR folks quickly pointed her at me because they knew I had an annoying pain in my neck.

Seeing as Dr. Lindsey applies principles of sports science, ergonomics, and performance medicine to gaming setups and actual Esports athletes, I was hoping for some technical, in-depth advice. Instead, she simply asked, "Do you have more than one monitor?"

"Yeah," I said, "I have one main one, and then a vertical one over on the right-hand side for Slack, Spotify, and other smaller apps when I'm working."

"And your pain is on which side?" she asked.

"You should try and put your secondary monitor up above your main one," Dr. Lindsey said with a smile. "That way, you won't be constantly craning your neck to the right and holding so much tension on that side".

I paused for a moment as I heard smirks emerging in the group. My eyebrows dropped, my eyes squinted. There's no way it's that simple, I thought to myself. Laughing it off, I retorted, "You sound crazy right now."

It was probably very disrespectful, but months later, after Secretlab called my bluff and supplied me with its various monitor arms to try, I feel like a total idiot.

Luckily, Dr. Lindsey took my feedback with great humour (even referring to me as a Celtic Jon Snow at one point), but for the record, I'd like to formally apologise for not taking her word as bond.

Turns out, stacking one monitor on top of the other made a world of difference, and despite the higher cost of Secretlab's vertical monitor stand, it's something I'd highly recommend to anyone who has more than one monitor on their gaming desk and struggles with similar pain to me. Lifting your head up to look at a monitor above your main eyeline is a much healthier repeated movement than constantly looking over to one direction - and no matter how good their head and neck support is, none of the best gaming chairs will change that.

I've now been using this monitor configuration for at least five or six months, and the difference in the neck pain I carry is massive. Thankfully, even though I don't own a Secretlab Magnus desk, I'm still able to make the brand's monitor arms work for me because they're compatible with other worktops so long as they meet the minimum thickness requirements for clamping them down securely.

Now, it should be said that alongside this monitor change, I've been doing a lot of exercise and gym work, which has no doubt done just as much to help things, so keep that in mind. I'm a firm believer that no one desk, monitor arm, or gaming chair is enough to cure your aches and pains without you putting in work alongside them.

Since originally taking on the vertical monitor stand and attaching both of my monitors to it, I've taken on a heavier OLED monitor as my main one, so I've also had to incorporate Secretlab's Heavy Duty Monitor Arm (also discounted in the Black Friday sale) to accommodate more than an 8kg load. It's a real shame you can't mix and match these. It'd be really cool if you could attach the stronger arm from the Heavy Duty variant to the vertical monitor stand, for example. Still, I can understand why the two aren't physically compatible.

The only other hesitation I have about Secretlab's vertical monitor stand is that it's expensive. For context, there are plenty listed at Amazon, like Standopia's and AVLT's which come in at $79.99 at Amazon and $99.99 at Amazon respectively.

Yes, with Secretlab's, you can attach all sorts to it if you wish. With room for four Doc Ock-like limbs extending out from it, you could have four monitors like a stock broker, two monitors and a tablet or music stand of some description, maybe a camera, or whatever you can make work. But even grabbing it with just two arms, it's a very pricey desk attachment. That's why I've chosen my moment to recommend it to you a little cheaper during Secretlab's Black Friday sale. If your budget can stretch to this monitor configuration with its small discount, I'd recommend it. Especially with Secretlab's build quality giving you peace of mind. If not, there are loads of cheaper alternatives linked below.

#3730. Arcade Archives TX-1 V.8 launches November 19

Arcade Archives 2 TX-1 V.8 will launch for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series, and Switch 2, and Arcade Archives TX-1 V.8 for PlayStation 4 and Switch, on November 19, developer Hamster announced. The Arcade Archives 2 version will cost $9.99 / 1,100 yen, while Arcade Archives version will cost $7.99 / 837 yen. An upgrade from Arcade Archives to Arcade Archives 2 will be available for $2.99 / 330 yen.

Here is an overview of the game, via Hamster:

TX-1 V.8 is a racing game released by TATSUMI in 1984.

The popular TX-1 has returned, featuring a variety of upgrades to make the game even easier to play!

You can now recover if your car rolls over or spins out, and it’s even possible to jump right over opponents ahead of you.

The eight countries featured in the Grand Prix stages are all new! Enjoy the fresh scenery of each location as you race toward the finish line!

The Arcade Archives series is developed with the concept of faithfully reproducing classic arcade games. It also includes convenient features such as difficulty and screen settings, rewind, rapid-fire, and multiple save slots. In addition, players can compete for the best scores with players around the world through online rankings.

Arcade Archives 2 series introduces a brand-new mode called Time Attack Mode, in addition to the Original Mode, Hi Score Mode, and Caravan Mode from Arcade Archives. Time Attack Mode focuses on how quickly you can complete the game, regardless of the score you achieve.

What’s more, with VRR (Variable Refresh Rate) support, the gameplay can be reproduced even more accurately, closer to the original arcade experience.

Please enjoy these iconic arcade games that defined an era with the Arcade Archives series!

#3729. The latest GTA 6 leak comes in the form of a 34-song tracklist for GTA 6: The Album, featuring Dua Lipa, Lana Del Rey, Rina Sawayama, and more

We are now just four days away from the release of GTA 6 on Xbox Series X/S and PS5, but the proximity to the much-anticipated launch date isn't stemming the tide of leaks that has been plaguing the game for much of the past year. Yesterday, a new video - seemingly from a record store that received vinyl records of the soundtrack early - showed off the full 34-song tracklist for the game.

Thanks to the listing printed on the back of Grand Theft Auto 6: The Album vinyl, we have a better idea of the licensed music that'll appear in-game. Travis Scott, Rina Sawayama, Cardi B, Pinkpantheress, SZA, Keith Richards, Dua Lipa, Jennie, Lana Del Rey, Zara Larsson are just some of the names that make up the impressive list. We know about a few of these tracks from September's announcement of the record, but only six tracks were revealed then, not the whole list.

Take a look at the full track listing below:

You can expect to hear these tracks on the radio - alongside many more, no doubt - and deployed at curated times during cutscenes or in missions, to really tie together the vibe of the city. This is something Vice City did remarkably well its roster of 80s tracks, and I can't wait to see how Rockstar has used more contemporary music in the same way here.

Of course, there have been a lot of Grand Theft Auto 6 leaks in the run-up to the game's launch. Another recent example is the full game's map which seemingly leaked online thanks to the £350 collector's edition on show in a UK department store. Then there were all the leaks from a group calling itself CyberLeek, which shared unofficial gameplay and map details over the course of a few weeks, before Rockstar had even revealed much gameplay itself.

Amongst all this, Rockstar has been embroiled in legal action after it was accused of union busting following the firing of over 30 employees. The case's conclusion will be determined this week, as the game goes on sale.

#3728. Sony defeat $2.6 billion UK class action lawsuit which argued PlayStation's dominant market position fuels "excessive and unfair" game prices

It's a joyous day for lawyers representing plucky little game and console makers Sony. A UK class action lawsuit which accused the company of using the PlayStation Store's dominant market position to fuel "excessive and unfair" prices for digital games has been dismissed in its entirety by the Competition Appeal Tribunal in London.

As reported by Reuters and The Game Business, the body ruled that the lawsuit - brought by Alex Neill on behalf of folks who bought digital games on PlayStation between August 2016 and February 2026 - failed to establish that Sony had infringed competition law.

The lawsuit claimed that PlayStation's dominant position when it comes to selling digital games on its platforms via the PlayStation Store subjected consumers to "excessive and unfair prices", as a result of terms and a 30% commission fee levied against developers. Neill and co argued owning a PlayStation traps game buyers within a competitionless ecosystem, thereby impacting their ability to seek out a better deal.

It's quite similar to the arguments which have been made against Valve in similar lawsuits concerning the Steam overlords' dominance over the PC game buying space, though a key distinction is that there is some competition on PC via the likes of the Epic store and GOG. How effective some of that competition can be in practice is a different kettle of fish, but the options are there.

In a judgement that could potentially factor into the responses to any similar lawsuits against Valve or other PC storefronts going forwards, the tribunal ruled that Sony compete in a wider ‘systems market’ against Xbox, Nintendo and PC, with PlayStation having no legal duty under competition law to allow third-party stores onto their platform as competition closer to home. The latter the tribunal noted would be expensive, complex and come with potential security ramifications.

As if that wasn't enough, the body ruled that as far as the pricing being unfair went, Neill hadn't proven that Sony’s profit margins were excessive and declared there was no evidence the presence of rival storefronts on PlayStation would've seen prices come down. That's essentially the word NO written in the largest font possible on a sheet of paper the size of a table, then.

Every lawsuit's different, especially when filed in different countries, but if I was one of the other class action suits against Sony or another big game seller on the go at the moment, I'd maybe not be feeling so hot right now. On the other hand, perhaps seeing what the tribunal judged Neill not to have provided suffiencient evidence for might aid those other efforts in formulating their arguments ready to face the scrutiny of government bodies and corporate law-talkers.

The Game Awards has announced its nominations slate for 2026, revealing that Grand Theft Auto 6 is this year's most-nominated game. Rockstar's hotly anticipated crime epic has secured eight nominations including Game of the Year, for which it'll be competing with games including Resident Evil Requiem, Control Resonant, and The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time.

Now you—and the countless other people preparing to argue about this online—may have noticed that GTA 6 has been nominated for a number of awards despite the fact that it hasn't been released yet. In a press release, The Game Awards notes that jurors were in some cases provided with early access to enable awards consideration.

"The nominees for The Game Awards are selected by a global jury of over 160 media publications and creator outlets around the world, who may be provided with advance or pre-release access to games for critical evaluation," The Game Awards said.

In a Variety interview last week, Game Awards host and co-creator Geoff Keighley refuted speculation that TGA 2026 eligibility deadlines had been sculpted to allow GTA 6 to have a shot for this year's nominations.

"There was a thing a few weeks ago where everyone thought that we had changed our dates to accommodate GTA, and it's like, no, actually our dates have been very set every year. It's the same calendar that we have," Keighley said. "I don't know this, but I'm sure some of these companies consider that when they're looking at their release calendars."

You can view and vote on the Game Awards nominees at the TGA website—but it's been crashing consistently since the nominees were announced, so we've collected all the nominees below. The Game Awards airs at 7:30 pm ET / 4:30 pm PT on Thursday, December 12 on Twitch and YouTube.
